records.locationNote: Seoul is listed on the global network map.
records.product: Website CDN · Free, Pro, Business, Contract
records.planNote: CDN is included across plans. Network Prioritization is a Contract feature; the public plans do not promise Seoul routing for a particular tier.
records.pricingNote: Pro is $20/mo annually or $25 monthly; Business is $200/mo annually or $250 monthly. No separate Korean website-CDN rate is published. Contract pricing is custom.

sources.label: Network map
sources.evidence: The current Asia data-center list includes Seoul, KR.

sources.label: Plans
sources.evidence: Website CDN appears under Free, Pro, Business and Contract. Network Prioritization is available on Contract, with dashes for the three self-service tiers. Published monthly/annual-billing prices are $0, $25/$20 and $250/$200; Contract is custom. No city-specific entitlement is given.

sources.label: Geographic traffic routing
sources.evidence: Cloudflare explains that Anycast requests can reach a location other than the geographically nearest one and that reliability can take precedence over local delivery.

limitations: Seoul presence does not establish a Seoul path for Free, Pro or Business traffic. No ISP-specific path was measured.
Contract Network Prioritization is not presented here as a guarantee of a specific city.

records.locationNote: Seoul is on Standard; it is not listed as a Volume location.
records.planNote: Choose Standard and keep Asia & Oceania enabled. Volume uses a smaller network; its lower price does not include a listed Seoul PoP.
records.pricingNote: Asia & Oceania delivery rate, with a $1 monthly minimum and no CDN request fees. Volume starts at $0.005/GB for the first 500 TB, with a different footprint.

sources.label: Network map
sources.evidence: The city list includes Seoul as a Standard location. The Volume markers in Asia are Hong Kong, Singapore and Tokyo; Seoul has no Volume marker.

sources.label: CDN tier documentation
sources.evidence: Standard accesses the full network; Volume uses ten selected PoPs. Standard Asia & Oceania costs $0.03/GB. A Pull Zone's Pricing & Routing settings select the tier and enable or disable pricing regions.

sources.label: Pricing
sources.evidence: Lists Standard Asia & Oceania at $0.03/GB, Volume first 500 TB at $0.005/GB, a $1 monthly minimum and no request fees.

limitations: The network list establishes tier coverage, not a measured path from a Korean ISP.
Volume pricing above 1 PB differs between the pricing page and documentation; that band is not quoted here.

records.locationNote: Seoul is listed in the current CDN status components.
records.planNote: The new PAYG plan includes 210+ PoPs. Existing Free, Start and Pro accounts must switch during the initial rollout; their old plan should not be assumed to have PAYG coverage.
records.pricingNote: PAYG's first paid band runs above 1 TB through 500 TB/month. Requests above 1 billion cost €0.75/million. No Korean surcharge is listed; VAT is excluded.

sources.label: CDN status components
sources.evidence: The public page's server-rendered component tree, fetched on 2026-10-10, contains Gcore > CDN > Asia & Pacific > Seoul, South Korea with status OPERATIONAL. The separate Hosting > Seoul (KX) component was not used as CDN evidence.

sources.label: PAYG launch and migration
sources.evidence: September 25, 2026 announcement replaces Free, Start and Pro with PAYG for new customers, giving every self-service customer access to 210+ PoPs and 1 TB free monthly. Existing accounts can opt in and are not moved automatically initially. Progressive usage bands: above 1 TB–500 TB €0.01/GB; 500 TB–1 PB €0.008; 1–2 PB €0.0065; above 2 PB €0.005.

sources.label: CDN pricing
sources.evidence: Current English pricing table gives PAYG and Enterprise 210+ PoPs; PAYG includes 1 TB monthly, €0.01/GB overage, €0.75/million requests above 1 billion, excluding VAT. It does not publish a South Korea surcharge.

limitations: The English PAYG pages are newer than localized pages that still show the legacy Free/Start/Pro plans.
No route from KT, SK Broadband or LG U+ was measured; published PoP access is not a city-selection guarantee.

records.locationNote: Seoul is listed as an active PoP, outside the Coming soon list.
records.planNote: Full Site Delivery has a recurring free allowance and usage pricing. South Korea is a separate billing region from Asia; no Seoul-only routing commitment is published on the pricing page.
records.pricingNote: After 100 GB free, South Korea is $0.28/GB through 10 TB/month, then $0.24/GB for the next 10 TB. After 1 million free requests, the first paid request band is $0.01/10,000. High-volume pricing is custom.

sources.label: Network map
sources.evidence: Network map updated June 30, 2026 lists Seoul under Asia; planned locations are in a separate Coming soon list.

sources.label: Full Site Delivery pricing
sources.evidence: Full Site Delivery bandwidth table bills per GB by region: 0–100 GB free, South Korea $0.28 for 100 GB–10 TB and $0.24 for the next 10 TB. General Asia is $0.19 and $0.14 respectively. Requests: first million free, then $0.01/10,000 through 100 million, with a lower next band.

limitations: Listed prices are public Full Site Delivery rates, not negotiated media-delivery quotes.
Seoul listing and regional billing do not verify the edge selected for a particular visitor.

records.locationNote: AWS lists ten CloudFront PoPs in Seoul.
records.product: PAYG: Price Class 200 or All · flat-rate plans
records.planNote: For PAYG, South Korea is included in Price Class 200 and All, and excluded from 100. Flat-rate plans include the global CDN; sustained excess usage can lead to more distant delivery.
records.pricingNote: PAYG: 1 TB and 10M requests free monthly, then $0.120/GB for the next 9 TB from the Korea pricing region; HTTPS $0.012/10,000 and HTTP $0.009/10,000. Separate flat-rate plans start at Free $0 and Pro $15/mo.

sources.label: CloudFront locations
sources.evidence: The CloudFront Points of Presence list gives South Korea: Seoul (10), distinct from AWS regions and regional edge caches.

sources.label: PAYG pricing and price classes
sources.evidence: South Korea's shared APAC region includes 1 TB free, next 9 TB $0.120/GB and next 40 TB $0.100/GB. First 10M HTTP(S) requests free; thereafter HTTP $0.009 and HTTPS $0.012 per 10,000. South Korea is Yes for Price Class All/200 and excluded for 100. An occasional out-of-class delivery is billed at the selected class's cheapest region.

sources.label: Flat-rate pricing
sources.evidence: Flat-rate plans include the global CloudFront CDN. Monthly entry tiers are Free $0 and Pro $15; these are distinct from PAYG per-GB charges.

sources.label: Flat-rate usage allowances
sources.evidence: Free includes 100 GB and 1M requests monthly; Pro includes 50 TB and 10M. No overage fees, but substantial continuing excess can cause fewer or more distant edge locations or performance adjustments. Historical usage can affect eligibility.

limitations: Price Class 100 can occasionally use an out-of-class edge; this does not make Seoul part of its documented coverage.
PAYG allowances and flat-rate allowances are separate offers; the $0.120/GB headline applies only to PAYG.
The published Seoul PoP count is not a measurement of Korean ISP routing.
